$schema: manifest of the static media corpus. sha256 + sizeBytes are filled by fixtures/bake.mjs after generation; commit this file (media itself is git-ignored). Asset ids are canonical and MUST match scenarios + golden filenames exactly. Every entry declares `source` (generated|fetched|captured|provided) and `sizeBucket` (empty|micro|tiny|small|medium|large|huge|massive) per test-instructions.md §5.3/§5.4. For `provided` assets the bake CANNOT make/fetch them deterministically: keep the entry, set sha256/sizeBytes null until dropped in at fixtures/media/<id>, and the bake prints a MISSING ASSETS block (drop path + where to obtain + expected size/sha256).

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1920x1080@30 30s + sine 48k stereo, libx264 yuv420p CRF20 -g 60 closed GOP, AAC 128k, +faststart, -fflags +bitexact
assets.notes: Baseline H.264/AAC progressive MP4. Workhorse for probe/demux/remux/transcode/decode/trim. medium bucket (~10-30 MB) default workhorse.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 3840x2160@30 10s + sine 48k stereo, libx264 yuv420p CRF24 -g 60 level 5.2, AAC 128k, +faststart
assets.notes: 4K stress for memory/throughput + high-level decode. May NA(browser) where 4K decode session unavailable.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1920x1080@30 10s + sine 48k stereo, libx265 yuv420p CRF24 -tag:v hvc1, AAC 128k, +faststart
assets.notes: HEVC in MP4 (hvc1). Decode support is browser/platform dependent (NA(browser) expected on Firefox/WebKit-no-HW).

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1920x1080@30 10s, libx264 -bf 3 -b_strategy 2 open-GOP (no -g forced IDR), pts!=dts reorder, AAC 128k, +faststart
assets.notes: B-frame reorder / open GOP: exercises pts vs dts demux and decode reordering.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 base 30fps then setpts to irregular timestamps (VFR) via -vsync vfr + setpts, libx264, AAC 128k, +faststart
assets.notes: Variable frame rate: irregular packet PTS spacing. Tests VFR-aware seek/probe duration.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1280x720@30 10s, libx264, then -metadata:s:v rotate=90 (display matrix), AAC 128k, +faststart
assets.notes: Rotation display-matrix metadata. Decoded frames must be presented rotated (display size swap).

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1280x720@30 10s video + two distinct sine audio tracks (440Hz, 880Hz) mapped as separate AAC streams, +faststart
assets.notes: Multiple audio tracks: track-layout demux + track selection.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1920x1080@30 5s + sine 48k stereo, libx264, AAC 128k, -f mov
assets.notes: QuickTime MOV container variant of the H.264/AAC baseline.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1920x1080@30 10s + sine 48k stereo, libvpx-vp9 -b:v 0 -crf 32 -row-mt 1, libopus 96k, -f webm
assets.notes: VP9/Opus WebM. Reference WebM video path.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1280x720@30 10s + sine 48k stereo, libvpx (vp8) -b:v 1M, libvorbis q4, -f webm
assets.notes: VP8/Vorbis WebM. Older codec pair; Vorbis has no WebCodecs decode string.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1280x720@30 5s + sine 48k stereo, libsvtav1 -crf 35 -preset 8, libopus 96k, -f webm
assets.notes: AV1/Opus WebM. Software-decoded where no HW; NA(browser) if AV1 decode absent.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 with generated alpha (format=yuva420p via geq/alpha ramp) 640x480@30 5s, libvpx-vp9 -pix_fmt yuva420p (alpha channel), -auto-alt-ref 0, -f webm
assets.notes: VP9 with alpha plane. alpha-plane oracle compares the alpha channel separately. NA(browser) if alpha decode unsupported.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1280x720@30 10s + sine, libx264, AAC, -f matroska
assets.notes: H.264 inside Matroska: cross-container demux/remux (mkv in, mp4 out).

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1280x720@30 10s + sine, libx264 -bsf:v h264_mp4toannexb, AAC -bsf:a aac_adtstoasc, -f mpegts
assets.notes: MPEG-TS (Annex-B H.264 + ADTS AAC). PTS/PCR demux; remux to MP4.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg ... -f hls -hls_time 2 -hls_playlist_type vod -hls_segment_filename hls_vod_%03d.ts hls_vod.m3u8 (playlist + sibling .ts segments)
assets.notes: Unencrypted HLS VOD: playlist + TS segments. sha256/size are of the .m3u8 playlist; segments are siblings (each in manifest as hls_vod_NNN.ts is NOT separately listed — bake records them in golden notes). sizeBucket reflects the playlist; the segment set totals ~small.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg -hls_key_info_file key_info -f hls (AES-128 segment encryption). KEY URI + IV in playlist; key bytes + IV recorded in golden for the decrypt oracle.
assets.notes: AES-128 encrypted HLS. ffmpeg 8 supports -hls_key_info_file natively (no Bento4 needed). If key generation unavailable in the bake env, recorded as SKIPPED with reason.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg -encryption_scheme cenc-aes-ctr -encryption_key <hex> -encryption_kid <hex> over the H.264/AAC baseline fragmented MP4. Key/KID/IV recorded in golden for decrypt oracle.
assets.notes: CENC AES-CTR (cenc) encrypted MP4. ffmpeg muxer supports -encryption_scheme cenc-aes-ctr. If unsupported in bake env, SKIPPED with reason; decrypt oracle then NA.

assets.genMethod: cbcs pattern encryption (AES-CBC w/ pattern). ffmpeg mov muxer -encryption_scheme cenc-aes-ctr only covers ctr; cbcs requires shaka/Bento4 (mp4encrypt --method MPEG-CENC scheme cbcs).
assets.acquire: If Bento4 (mp4encrypt) or shaka packager is installed on the bake host, bake.mjs generates cenc_cbcs.mp4 automatically (source effectively becomes generated) — install one and re-run `bun fixtures/bake.mjs cenc_cbcs.mp4`. Otherwise produce it manually: `mp4encrypt --method MPEG-CENC --encryption-scheme cbcs --key 1:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef:random --property 1:KID:abcdef00112233445566778899aabbcc <plain_h264_aac.mp4> fixtures/media/cenc_cbcs.mp4`, where <plain_h264_aac.mp4> is the cenc_ctr.mp4 cleartext baseline (libx264 yuv420p + AAC, +faststart). Record key/KID into fixtures/golden/cenc_cbcs.mp4.keys.json for the decrypt oracle.
assets.notes: CENC cbcs (pattern) encrypted MP4. ffmpeg cannot emit cbcs; needs Bento4/shaka. provided (SKIPPED with reason / MISSING ASSETS) when those binaries are absent; decrypt oracle then NA(asset-missing).

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 48k stereo 5s, -c:a pcm_s16le, -f wav
assets.notes: 16-bit little-endian PCM WAV. Baseline PCM.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 48k stereo 5s, -c:a pcm_s24le, -f wav
assets.notes: 24-bit PCM WAV. Tests 24-bit sample handling in audio-dsp.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 48k stereo 5s, -c:a pcm_f32le, -f wav
assets.notes: 32-bit float PCM WAV.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 48k stereo 5s, -c:a pcm_s16be, -f aiff (big-endian PCM; WAVE/RIFF cannot carry pcm_s16be, AIFF is the natural big-endian PCM container)
assets.notes: Big-endian 16-bit PCM in AIFF. Byte-order edge case for audio-dsp/robustness. (Was wav_s16be.wav: pcm_s16be is invalid in WAVE; moved to AIFF.)

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 44.1k stereo 10s, libmp3lame VBR (-q:a 2) which writes a Xing/Info header (TOC + frame count)
assets.notes: VBR MP3 with Xing header (seek TOC present).

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 44.1k stereo 10s, libmp3lame CBR (-b:a 128k) with -write_xing 0 (no Xing/TOC)
assets.notes: CBR MP3 without Xing TOC: duration/seek must be derived from byte rate.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 48k stereo 10s, -c:a flac (default writes a SEEKTABLE metadata block)
assets.notes: FLAC WITH SEEKTABLE.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 48k stereo 10s, -c:a flac then strip SEEKTABLE via -map_metadata -1 + metaflac --remove (or -frame_size to suppress); if no metaflac, encode and note SEEKTABLE may persist.
assets.notes: FLAC WITHOUT SEEKTABLE: seek must scan frames. Removal of SEEKTABLE needs metaflac; if absent, recorded with a caveat.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 48k stereo 10s, -c:a aac -f adts (raw ADTS stream)
assets.notes: Raw ADTS AAC. Headerless-container probing of frame headers.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 48k stereo 10s, libopus 96k, -f ogg
assets.notes: Opus in OGG.

assets.genMethod: IN-BROWSER MediaRecorder capture (canvas.captureStream + MediaRecorder, video/webm). Cannot be produced by ffmpeg: MediaRecorder WebM is non-seekable / cluster-only / lacks a cues/duration header. Baked by a one-time browser pass (see bake.mjs RECORDER_NOTE).
assets.acquire: Open fixtures/tools/record-fixture.html in a browser, click Record (~3s), save the download as fixtures/media/recorder_headerless.webm, then re-run `bun fixtures/bake.mjs recorder_headerless.webm` to checksum it.
assets.notes: Headerless/streaming MediaRecorder WebM. NOT faked by ffmpeg. Produced via tools/record-fixture.html in a browser, then dropped into fixtures/media/. bake.mjs records it as SKIPPED(browser-capture) until present.

assets.genMethod: Zero-payload WAV: a valid 44-byte RIFF/WAVE header with a 0-length data chunk (ffmpeg sine duration 0 -c:a pcm_s16le -f wav). Distinct from zero_length.mp4 (which is a true 0-byte file): this one is a *structurally valid but empty-media* container, exercising the 'no samples' edge separately from the 'no bytes' edge.
assets.notes: empty bucket (structurally-valid container, zero media). probe should report duration 0 / no samples without crashing; demux yields 0 packets.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 320x240@1 -frames:v 1, libx264 yuv420p, +faststart, no audio. A single-keyframe ~1 KB MP4. Header/edge robustness + minimal-decode latency.
assets.notes: micro bucket (~1 KB). Exactly one keyframe; smallest valid playable MP4 in the corpus. probe/demux/decode-1-frame edge.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 44.1k mono 0.1s, AAC 32k, -f mp4 (m4a). ~1-2 KB audio MP4 for micro-bucket audio probe/demux latency.
assets.notes: micro bucket audio (~1-2 KB). Few AAC frames; init-overhead-dominated probe latency.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 640x360@30 2s + sine 48k stereo, libx264 yuv420p CRF26 -g 60, AAC 96k, +faststart. ~100 KB. probe/demux latency + init overhead at the tiny scale.
assets.notes: tiny bucket (~100 KB) 360p MP4. Size-ladder representative for the MP4/H.264 family.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 640x360@30 2s + sine 48k stereo, libvpx-vp9 -b:v 0 -crf 40 -row-mt 1, libopus 64k, -f webm. ~100 KB. Size-ladder tiny for the WebM/VP9 family (crosses the size axis with the format axis).
assets.notes: tiny bucket (~100 KB) 360p WebM. Pairs with tiny_h264_360p_2s.mp4 so the tiny rung covers both major container/codec families.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1920x1080@30 120s + sine 48k stereo, libx264 yuv420p CRF23 -g 60 closed GOP, AAC 128k, +faststart. ~100-150 MB. Sustained throughput + memory for the MP4/H.264 family. Slow to generate.
assets.notes: large bucket (~100 MB) 1080p H.264 MP4. Sustained metadata-extract / packet-iterate / convert throughput; memory pressure.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1920x1080@30 120s + sine 48k stereo, libvpx-vp9 -b:v 0 -crf 34 -row-mt 1 -deadline good -cpu-used 5 -g 60, libopus 96k, -f webm. ~80-150 MB. Large WebM/VP9 so the large rung crosses container/codec. VERY slow to generate (VP9 sw encode of 120s 1080p).
assets.notes: large bucket (~100 MB) 1080p VP9 WebM. Pairs with large_h264_1080p_120s.mp4 so the large rung covers both major families. Generation is slow; use --skip-longform or --subset to defer.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1920x1080@30 600s (10 min) + sine 48k stereo, libx264 yuv420p CRF23 -g 60 closed GOP, AAC 128k, -f mov +faststart. Targets ~500-700 MB to mirror the BigBuckBunny1080pH264.mov 'huge' bucket. This is the SELF-CONTAINED, deterministic, network-free 'big read' asset (BigBuckBunny-style 1080p H.264 .mov) the suite always has. VERY slow + large to generate; gated by --skip-longform.
assets.notes: huge bucket (~500-700 MB) self-contained big-read asset: large 1080p H.264 .mov for metadata-extract / packet-iterate / convert throughput at scale (mirrors Mediabunny's published-chart input shape). Generated offline, no network needed — always present after a full bake. The REAL BigBuckBunny1080pH264.mov is additionally available as the 'provided' entry big_buck_bunny_1080p_h264.mov for published-chart parity.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1920x1080@30 240s (4 min) + sine 48k stereo, libvpx-vp9 -b:v 0 -crf 34 -row-mt 1 -deadline good -cpu-used 5 -g 60, libopus 96k, -f webm. Targets ~500-700 MB to land in the 'huge' band. WebM/VP9 twin of huge_h264_1080p_600s.mov so the huge rung crosses BOTH major container/codec families (§5.3 worked example). VERY slow (VP9 sw encode of long 1080p); gated by --skip-longform.
assets.notes: huge bucket (~500-700 MB) WebM/VP9 big-read twin. §5.3 requires at least one asset per major container/codec per bucket — this pairs with huge_h264_1080p_600s.mov so the size axis crosses the format axis at the huge rung. Generated offline; --skip-longform omits it during quick bakes.

assets.genMethod: REAL BigBuckBunny1080pH264.mov (~691 MiB) — Mediabunny's own published-benchmark input (test-instructions.md §5.1 'Big read file', §5.3 'huge' bucket). The bake CANNOT fetch a sha256-pinned copy: the exact 691 MiB file Mediabunny benchmarks is an internal/private asset with no published checksum, so a TOFU download cannot be honestly 'pinned'. It is therefore source:'provided' (drop-in) rather than fetched. The synthetic huge_h264_1080p_600s.mov covers the same big-read role deterministically and is always present; THIS asset is the optional published-chart-parity twin.
assets.acquire: Obtain the real Big Buck Bunny 1080p H.264 .mov (Blender Foundation, CC-BY 3.0). Canonical source: https://download.blender.org/peach/bigbuckbunny_movies/big_buck_bunny_1080p_h264.mov (~691 MiB; the Blender Peach mirror — this is the same content Mediabunny benchmarks). Download it, then `shasum -a 256 big_buck_bunny_1080p_h264.mov` to compute its sha256, drop it at fixtures/media/big_buck_bunny_1080p_h264.mov, record that sha256 + sizeBytes into this manifest entry, and re-run `bun fixtures/bake.mjs big_buck_bunny_1080p_h264.mov --golden-only` to derive golden. ALTERNATIVELY, to make the bake auto-fetch it, set the env var BBB_MOV_SHA256=<the sha256 you trust> and re-run the bake: bake.mjs will download from sourceUrl, verify against BBB_MOV_SHA256, and on match treat it as fetched (offline-once). Without a trusted sha256 the bake will NOT silently download (no unpinned TOFU).
assets.notes: huge bucket / big-read PARITY asset: the actual file behind Mediabunny's published 1080p H.264 .mov chart. provided (drop-in or pin-then-fetch via BBB_MOV_SHA256). Until present, big-read parity cases are NA(asset-missing); the deterministic huge_h264_1080p_600s.mov keeps the huge rung populated regardless. expectedSizeBytes ~691 MiB is approximate (Blender Peach mirror); verify after download.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 48k mono 3600s, AAC 64k, -f mp4 (m4a). Long duration for streaming/seek/memory stress.
assets.notes: Multi-hour audio (1h, ~28 MB at 64k). Many-samples / long-duration seek + streaming. Large; generation is slow. Use --skip-longform or --subset to skip during quick bakes.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1920x1080@30 7200s (2h) + sine 48k mono, libx264 yuv420p -b:v 1200k (low bitrate, capped) -g 60 closed GOP, AAC 64k, +faststart. Low-bitrate long-form so the file lands ~1-1.4 GB / many-thousand-sample with bounded encode time. Lazy-read / streaming / peak-memory / OOM-resistance + many-samples sample-table stress. VERY slow + very large; gated by --skip-longform.
assets.notes: massive bucket (~1-1.4 GB, 2h, ~216k video frames) low-bitrate 1080p. Exercises lazy/partial reading, streaming demux, peak-memory and OOM-resistance, and many-thousand-sample sample-table parsing. Generated offline but slow; --skip-longform omits it. Real multi-hour camera/broadcast captures may additionally be supplied as 'provided'.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1920x1080@30 7200s (2h) + sine 48k mono, libvpx-vp9 -b:v 700k -maxrate 800k -bufsize 1600k (low bitrate, capped) -row-mt 1 -deadline good -cpu-used 5 -g 60, libopus 64k, -f webm. Low-bitrate long-form so the file lands ~1-1.4 GB / many-thousand-sample with bounded encode time. WebM/VP9 twin of massive_h264_1080p_2h.mp4 so the massive rung crosses BOTH major families (§5.3). VERY slow + very large; gated by --skip-longform.
assets.notes: massive bucket (~1-1.4 GB, 2h) low-bitrate 1080p WebM/VP9 twin. Pairs with massive_h264_1080p_2h.mp4 so lazy-read / streaming / peak-memory / OOM-resistance + many-sample stress is exercised in both major container/codec families. Generated offline but slow; --skip-longform omits it.

assets.genMethod: Empty 0-byte file written directly (no ffmpeg). Degenerate input for graceful-failure oracle.
assets.notes: Zero-length file (true 0 bytes). Engines must fail gracefully (no crash/hang/OOM). Complements empty_audio.wav (valid-but-empty container).

assets.genMethod: Generate the H.264/AAC baseline (short), then truncate to ~60% of its bytes (head -c) so the moov/mdat is incomplete.
assets.notes: Truncated MP4 (incomplete moov/mdat). Robustness: graceful failure or partial-but-safe handling. micro-ish robustness rung.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 4x4@30 2s then -vf scale=1:1, libvpx-vp9 yuv420p -b:v 0 -crf 40, -f webm (video-only). libx264/yuv420p cannot encode 1x1 — VP9 carries the literal 1x1 honestly; the H.264-family degenerate twin is video_2x2_h264.mp4.
assets.notes: Deep edge (§A.16 '0x0 or 1x1 video'): a 1x1 VP9 WebM. Degenerate minimal dimensions; probe/decode must report 1x1 without divide-by-zero / aspect crashes. video-only (no audio track).

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 2x2@30 2s, libx264 yuv420p CRF30 -g 30 closed GOP, +faststart, no audio. Smallest EVEN-dimension H.264 (libx264 rejects 1x1 / odd dimensions under yuv420p). MP4/H.264 degenerate-size twin of video_1x1.webm.
assets.notes: Deep edge (§A.16 '0x0 or 1x1 video', H.264 family): 2x2 is the smallest valid even-dimension H.264. Pairs with video_1x1.webm so the tiny-dimension edge crosses both major families. video-only.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 320x240@240 2s, libx264 yuv420p CRF28 -g 240 closed GOP, +faststart, no audio. The high-fps end of §A.16 'extreme fps (1 fps, 240 fps)'.
assets.notes: Deep edge (§A.16 'extreme fps'): 240 fps video. avg_frame_rate must report 240; per-frame PTS spacing ~4.17 ms. The 1-fps end is covered by micro_h264_1frame.mp4 (rate=1). video-only.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1280x720@30 4s + sine 48k stereo, libx264 yuv420p + AAC 128k, -movflags +frag_keyframe+empty_moov+default_base_moof -f mp4. CMAF-style fragmented MP4: empty moov (init) + moof/mdat fragments (media), self-contained moofs.
assets.notes: Deep edge (§A.16 'fragmented/CMAF init+media split'): unencrypted fragmented MP4 so the fragmentation edge is isolated from encryption (cenc_ctr.mp4 is fragmented AND encrypted). Probe/demux must handle empty-moov + moof fragments and init/media separation.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 320x240@30 2s + sine, libx264 yuv420p + AAC, -movflags +faststart, -f mp4 written to a .webm-named file (the -f mp4 forces the MP4 muxer regardless of extension). The bytes begin with 'ftyp...' (ISOBMFF), NOT the EBML magic 1A45DFA3.
assets.notes: Deep edge (§A.16 'mismatched container/codec (h264 mislabeled)'): genuine H.264/MP4 bytes inside a file whose .webm extension LIES about the container. `container` here is the TRUE container (mp4); `declaredExtension` records the lie. The probe oracle must trust sniffed content over the extension/MIME. Golden meta is derived from the real (mp4) bytes.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 44.1k stereo 1.013s (non-frame-aligned), AAC 96k, -movflags +faststart -f mp4. AAC always carries encoder delay (priming) + end padding; the odd duration makes the padding non-trivial. iTunSMPB / edit-list gapless info present.
assets.notes: Deep edge (§A.16 'gapless audio (encoder delay/padding)'): the decoded sample count after trimming encoder delay + padding must match the nominal 1.013 s (no gap on loop). Tests whether the engine honors edit lists / iTunSMPB priming.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg sine 440Hz 48k 3s, -af pan=5.1|c0=c0|... (fan mono to 5.1), AAC 256k, -movflags +faststart -f mp4. A 6-channel (5.1) AAC track; the rest of the audio corpus is mono/stereo.
assets.notes: Deep edge (§A.16 'variable channel count'): 6-channel 5.1 AAC. Probe must report channels=6 / layout=5.1; downmix-to-stereo and channel-layout-aware DSP are exercised against a non-stereo source.

assets.genMethod: Two independently-timestamped MPEG-TS segments byte-concatenated: segA at t=0, segB muxed with -output_ts_offset 600 (-muxpreload 0 -muxdelay 0), so the joined stream's PTS jumps ~+597 s at the splice. TS is packet-boundary concatenable. Deterministic (no reliance on fragile 33-bit PCR-wrap emission).
assets.notes: Deep edge (§A.16 'timestamp wraparound / discontinuity (TS)'): a real forward PTS discontinuity at the segment splice. The demux oracle must tolerate the jump (no negative-duration, no hang, no OOM) — mirrors a PCR wrap / stream splice.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1 frame 640x480, -frames:v 1 -f image2 image.jpg
assets.notes: Image negative. A media engine should return a clean NA/error, never crash.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1 frame 640x480, -frames:v 1 image.png
assets.notes: PNG image negative.

assets.genMethod: ffmpeg testsrc2 1 frame 640x480, -frames:v 1 -c:v libwebp image.webp
assets.notes: WebP image negative (still image, not a WebM video).
